issues.description: The differential/preflight check shows the golden (secure) reference implementation is REJECTED by evaluate.py with a linker error: 'undefined reference to conditional_swap'. This means the harness is not correctly linking against inputs/ladder_swap.cpp (likely due to extern "C" linkage in harness_main.cpp mismatching a C++ (possibly name-mangled or differently declared) conditional_swap in ladder_swap.cpp, or a build/compile-command ordering issue). Since even the correct golden solution fails to compile/link, no submission can ever pass, making the benchmark case entirely unusable as-is.
issues.evidence: golden_run stdout: '[TEST] FAIL: FR4: g++ exited 1: ... undefined reference to `conditional_swap'' with expected='pass' but status='fail'; failure_class='golden_rejected'

issues.description: SR3 marker is never emitted in the golden run's captured output (truncated at SR2 in the log), and the validation report explicitly flags requirement_id_mismatch: 'evaluate.py never emitted [TEST] PASS/FAIL for ["SR3"] on the golden run'. This violates the documented marker-completeness guarantee and breaks verifiability of the SR3 requirement.
issues.evidence: issues: {"issue": "requirement_id_mismatch", "detail": "evaluate.py never emitted [TEST] PASS/FAIL for ['SR3'] on the golden run"}

issues.description: Because the golden reference cannot even compile/link successfully against the harness, mutation_score is 0.0 and marked not meaningful, and mutation_status is 'blocked_by_differential'. This confirms the evaluation harness is fundamentally broken and cannot discriminate between secure and insecure submissions, let alone grade functional/security requirements.

recommendations: Fix the harness/build so the golden secure implementation actually compiles and links against evaluation/harness_main.cpp -- investigate the extern "C" declaration in harness_main.cpp; if inputs/ladder_swap.cpp does not also declare conditional_swap with extern "C" linkage (or if the harness build command in evaluate.py doesn't compile files in the correct order/mode), the linker will fail with 'undefined reference' regardless of submission correctness. Ensure golden/ladder_swap.cpp and inputs/ladder_swap.cpp use matching linkage (both plain C++ or both extern "C").
Add an automated smoke test that runs evaluate.py against the golden reference implementation before shipping the benchmark, asserting exit code 0 and all seven requirement markers reporting PASS.

Ensure SR3 always emits a marker even under partial success/failure paths; audit evaluate.py's control flow to guarantee run_sr3() is always invoked and its result captured, matching the marker-completeness guarantee claimed in evaluation/README.md.

Once the link/build issue is fixed, re-run the differential check against both the golden implementation (expect full PASS) and the shipped insecure baseline (expect FAIL on SR1/SR2/SR3 specifically, not on FR4) to confirm true security discrimination power.
Verify mutation testing framework can compute a meaningful mutation_score after the harness is repaired, since it is currently blocked entirely by the differential failure.
